entries.justification: The command is a compile-time constant ('git rev-parse --show-toplevel') with no caller-supplied content; the shell is involved only because execSync takes a string, and no argument material is interpolated. The repository's policy for anything argument-bearing is execFileSync with an array.

This is the platform fetch bound as the DEFAULT TRANSPORT of the OpenRouter executor, not a request to an arbitrary host: the outbound URL guard of this transport restricts the request to the explicit openrouter.ai host allowlist over https, with redirects refused so no authorization is forwarded. The gate reports the BINDING; it does not and cannot verify that guard, which lives in the transport. The request itself is issued through the bound implementation, not through a literal fetch call, which is why the bare form of the rule could not see it.

This line selects the platform fetch as the default transport of the JEV decision client. The endpoint is constrained before the call by the client's own outbound guard, which requires an https URL whose host is in the configured allowlist. The gate reports the BINDING only and does not verify that guard. The line carries the binding twice (the type test and the selection), so the scanner reports two findings on it and two disclosures are required.

Second occurrence on the same line: the selection of the platform fetch as the default transport appears twice in that expression, so the scanner reports two findings on line 126 and this disclosure covers the second one. The disclosure is identical to the first because it is the same binding.

The specifier is a file URL the loader constructs from the --executor-module OPERATOR surface. The module's own header states that this argument is deliberately NOT confined to the repository and that loading it is code execution by design: the operator chooses the module. This disclosure therefore states the operator authority, not a confinement: the path-confinement primitive governs the CORPUS files (subject content, family and variant case files), which are read before the import, and the executor module itself is outside that boundary by design. The earlier justification of this entry claimed a confinement that does not exist here and was corrected on 2026-10-21 after an independent qualification.
